[Kim (2014)](https://aclanthology.org/D14-1181/) establishes ordered, contiguous word-window convolutions followed by max-over-time pooling; widths 3/4/5 are standard precedents. Filters distinguish token positions within each window, but global max pooling discards the positions and relative order of detected windows. [AllenNLP’s implementation](https://github.com/allenai/allennlp/blob/main/allennlp/modules/seq2vec_encoders/cnn_encoder.py) provides a stricter masking precedent: zero masked embeddings, apply valid convolution, exclude activations whose windows touch padding before max pooling. Its length-based mask assumes right padding; arbitrary or left padding requires constructing window validity directly from the token mask.

Implementation inference for widths 3/5: explicitly choose strict complete-window semantics or boundary-padded semantics. Under strict semantics, a window is valid only when all k tokens are real; physically pad tensors to at least width 5 so convolution executes, then return zero for branches with no valid windows. Consequently, fields shorter than k contribute nothing to that branch. Alternatively, symmetric zero padding of 1/2 tokens permits width-3/5 features on short fields; pool only outputs centered on real tokens and explicitly zero empty fields. These alternatives encode different hypotheses. For max pooling, mask invalid activations with negative infinity and handle all-invalid rows; for mean pooling, sum valid activations and divide by their valid count.

[Zhang and Wallace](https://arxiv.org/html/1510.03820) hold convolution architecture fixed when comparing pooling: global-average accuracy was 80.17/83.30 on CR/TREC versus approximately 83.8/91.5 for global max. This controls pooling capacity, but uses pretrained embeddings and does not establish superiority over parameter-matched token-mean encoders inside HSTU. Proposed controls: identical-CNN max versus mean pooling; parameter-matched mean-embedding MLP; identical CNN trained on shuffled tokens to isolate order. Keep each comparison within one jointly trained HSTU model per category.
